chunks: The two rak‘ahs that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله added on the day of al-Jumu‘ah are for the resident because of the two sermons with the Imam. So whoever prays on the day of al-Jumu‘ah outside of congregation, then let him pray it as four rak‘ahs, like Salat al-Zuhr on the rest of the days.

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: four rak‘ahs, as required when not prayed in congregation
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَانِ: the two units of prayer prescribed here for Jumu‘ah
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader with whom the Jumu‘ah prayer is performed
key_terms.الْخُطْبَتَيْنِ: the two sermons that accompany the congregational Jumu‘ah prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الظُّهْرِ: the noon prayer, used here as the legal equivalent when Jumu‘ah is not held congregationally
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, when the Jumu‘ah prayer is observed

ai.seo_question: Why is the Jumu‘ah prayer two rak‘ahs with the Imam but four rak‘ahs when prayed individually?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal basis for Jumu‘ah being two rak‘ahs when performed with the Imam and accompanied by the two sermons. If a person does not perform it in congregation, he should pray four rak‘ahs like the regular Zuhr prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1221 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:

"The two rak'ahs that The Prophet (sw) added on the day of Jumu’ah are for those who attend with the Imam because of the two sermons. Whoever prays on Jumu’ah but not in congregation should pray it as four rak'ahs, like the Dhuhr prayer on other days."
